Dialogues, videos, vocabulary building exercises and other materials are available and students are free to choose their preferred types of practice. 
The course offers learners the opportunity to develop practical communication skills and will enable learners to become independent users of English, and to be able to use English to communicate effectively in a variety of practical contexts.

Practical strategies to help learners achieve results in all areas of the exams - particularly speaking parts 1,2 and 3, listening and reading. Writing may be included at the students' request.
Students can hone their skills using past exam questions and topic prompts. Reading practice includes skimming and scanning, looking for key language within a text, inference, predicting what you will hear, repetition of answers, identifying synonyms and other ways of analysing a text. 
Learn how the exams are assessed and get tips on how to deal with common problems learners have while preparing.  
A series of classes is recommended to make the most of your preparation time and to perfect your skills.

teacher_info.about_teacher: In 2006, I began teaching English as a second language to international students at Western Michigan University. I have taught students from all over the world: Saudi Arabia, China, France, and the Dominican Republic are among some of the places my students call home.  I specialize in academic and professional English focused on speaking, listening, grammar, reading and writing. However, I have also worked with students developing basic vocabulary, pronunciation, and conversational skills. Although I am rooted in the United States, my greatest pleasure in teaching English comes from the connections I make to other lands and cultures through my students.
teacher_info.teaching_style: My general approach to language instruction is task-based.  Rather than focusing on discrete grammar points or lengthy vocabulary definitions, I ask my students to use and stretch their language skills by performing communicative tasks.  Example tasks might include creating a professional powerpoint or reading an article from a peer-review journal. The goal is to practice English in authentic, real-world situations. However, an understanding of grammar and vocabulary is important as well and are dealt with as needed in the context of communication. For example, I use the Academic Word List (AWL) to help draw attention to key words used in nearly all professions and university majors.

pro_course_detail.title: Reading & Writing English for Professional or Academic Purposes
pro_course_detail.description:
Develop your reading and writing skills and knowledge of high level vocabulary by working with real-world texts in task-oriented contexts.

This course is designed to help students reach their next level in English (e.g. from B2 to C1).  The total course takes approximately 36 lessons and covers several academic and professional topics, more than 100 high-level vocabulary words, and various grammar and pronunciation points along the way. 
Schedule a lesson today!

This course consists of 8 Units:
Each Unit consists of Five Phases:
Phase 1: Reading and Comprehension
Phase 2: Annotations and Deep Dive
Phase 3: Vocabulary Acquisition and Use
Phase 4: Summary and Response
Phase 5: Timed Test and Review
